hook: A Breakthrough Solution That Supports A Sharper & Clearer Vision Well Into Old Age
claim: OptiPlax is a once-a-day vision capsule with a proprietary blend that includes astaxanthin and several seaweeds and algae.
ing_note: The website lists these as part of the blend 'including' them; amounts aren't disclosed.
use: One capsule a day with 6–8 oz of water or another drink.
price_note: OptiPlax is sold as 2 bottles (+$9.99 shipping), 2+1 bottles or 3+3 bottles with free shipping; totals appear on the order page.
refund_note: For a refund you must return all bottles, empty or not, with the packing slip.
bonuses: 10 printable vision templates and a 30-second daily eye workout
A guide to exotic fruits for eyesight
checks: Astaxanthin is the one ingredient with some eye research: small trials suggest it may reduce eye strain and fatigue at 6–12 mg a day.
It doesn't contain lutein or zeaxanthin, the nutrients proven (in AREDS2) to slow advanced macular degeneration.
Three seaweeds add iodine, which can affect thyroid function.
Eye workouts don't improve refractive errors like short-sightedness.
verdict: OptiPlax has one plausible ingredient (astaxanthin, for eye fatigue) but lacks the nutrients with the strongest eye evidence. If your vision is changing, get an eye exam; glasses, cataract surgery and treatments for macular degeneration and glaucoma make a real difference.
